To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the incidence of AIDS-related lymphoma is increased in HIV-infected patients, that it is a highly aggressive disease with a poor prognosis, and that it is a major cause of death in HIV-infected individuals.
AIDS-related lymphoma and HIV-associated lymphoma are the same entity and that rituximah and CHOP is an effective schedule for AIDS-related lymphoma.

(1) the risk of AIDS related malignancies is increased during the pre- and post-AIDS period, (2) AIDS is necessary for most malignancies to develop in individuals with HIV, (3) the risk of HIV-associated non–AIDS-related malignancies does not substantially increase before inducing AIDS, (4) highly active antiretoviral therapy prevents immunosuppression and decreased incidences AIDS-defining malignancies but cannot eradicate HIV.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an HIV vaccine.
the use of the terms AIDS related and HIV associated.
the development of a novel approach to the development of a new class of HIV-associated malignancies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

AIDS-related lymphomas are the most common malignancies in individuals infected with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) and that they are more frequent and more aggressive in patients with AIDS, but that HIV-associated lymphomas are also more frequent and more malignant than lymphomas in the general population, and that they are not AIDS-defining cancers, but they are non–AIDS defining cancers.
rituximam and CHOP is a simple and highly effective regimen for both AIDS-related and non–AIDS-related lymphomas in patients infected with HIV.
AIDS-related lymphoma is a type of lymphoma occurring in AIDS patients and HIV-associated lymphoma is a lymphoma occurring in patients infected with HIV but without AIDS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AIDS related lymphoma is the term that is more correct, more comprehensive, and more inclusive.
AIDS is necessary but not sufficient to develop malignancies in individuals infected with human immunodeficiency virus.
AIDS related lymphoma is the lymphoma developing in individuals with AIDS, and HIV-associated lymphoma is the malignancy developing in individuals infected but not yet immunocompromised by HIV.
The main takeaway from our work is that
AIDS-related lymphoma is a different entity from non–AIDS-related lymphoma.
we need to be more careful with our terminology.
we should not forget that HIV-associated cancers are AIDS-related cancers.
